A.biggest_strength: Exceptional pedagogical clarity and visual design, combining an intuitive network topology diagram, packet animation, stacked latency comparison bars, and authentic dig-style wire formatting.
A.biggest_weakness: Does not demonstrate cross-domain cache reuse (such as how a cached .com TLD record accelerates a subsequent query for a different .com domain).

B.biggest_strength: Thorough supplementary technical notes and tables, including an insightful multi-domain caching comparison that demonstrates how cached TLD records benefit unrelated domains under the same TLD.
B.biggest_weakness: Cramped, low-contrast visual presentation with awkward controls that degrade significantly at mobile width, alongside inaccurate claims of real captured Cloudflare records for example.com.
factual_errors: Claims that www.example.com resolves to Cloudflare IP 104.20.23.154 via authoritative nameserver hera.ns.cloudflare.com and that these were 'real, captured with dig +norecurse on 16 Oct 2026'. In reality, example.com is an IANA-reserved domain (RFC 2606) pointing to 93.184.215.14 with authoritative nameservers a.iana-servers.net and b.iana-servers.net.
References a non-existent script ('Run node model.mjs --dig to compare them with the live servers again') in the figure caption.

structured_output.reasons: Page A is the clear winner because it presents the DNS resolution walk with outstanding pedagogical clarity, authentic protocol fidelity, and polished visual design. Its network topology diagram, traveling packet animation, wire-level dig messages, and stacked latency comparison bars make the mechanics of recursion, referrals, and cache hits immediately obvious to networking students. Page B provides commendable supplementary reference notes, but its sequence diagram and controls are visually cramped, difficult to operate on mobile devices, and marred by fabricated DNS records for example.com.
